title: Generalized Marginals of tie -Wigner Distribution nand Lagrangian Tomography
abstract: We develop a symplectic formulation of the Lagrangian Radon transform based on the transitive action of the symplectic group on the Lagrangian Grassmannian. This geometric framework naturally extends the classical notion of the marginals of the Wigner transform, viewed as elementary tomograms, to arbitrary Lagrangian subspaces. The resulting generalized tomography provides a unified treatment of position and momentum measurements related by symplectic rotations. As applications, we revisit the Pauli reconstruction problem and establish reconstruction formulas for density operators from generalized Lagrangian tomograms.
summary: This paper introduces a generalized Lagrangian Radon transform based on symplectic geometry to extend the concept of marginal measurements in quantum mechanics. It shows that by measuring projections (tomograms) along arbitrary Lagrangian subspaces, one can uniquely reconstruct the full quantum state's Wigner function or density operator. This provides a powerful mathematical tool for understanding phase-space tomography.
main_problem: The paper develops a symplectic formulation for the Lagrangian Radon transform to generalize the marginals of the Wigner distribution, providing a unified quantum tomography framework.
main_result: It establishes that generalized marginal measurements along arbitrary Lagrangian subspaces are sufficient to reconstruct the full density operator or Gaussian state in phase space.
method: The approach uses advanced harmonic analysis on the symplectic group $Sp(n)$ acting on the Lagrangian Grassmannian $	ext{Lag}(n)$, generalizing classical Radon transforms.
model_or_system: The theory applies to quantum states described by density operators ($ho$) and their Wigner representations ($W\psi$), operating in phase space $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.
key_observables: Generalized Lagrangian tomograms, the Wigner function $W\psi$, and the covariance matrix $\Sigma$.
important_parameters: The symplectic group structure, the dimension $n$ (related to degrees of freedom), and Planck's constant ($\hbar$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes sufficient smoothness conditions on the density operator for the Radon transform definitions to hold.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the symplectic geometry of the Lagrangian Radon transform, applying it first to Gaussian states (reconstruction formulas), and finally extending the concept to reconstruct general density operators via cross-Wigner distributions.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical underpinning for quantum state tomography, connecting fundamental concepts like Wigner functions and phase space measurements through rigorous geometric methods applicable to open quantum systems theory.
